```{r}
#| label: setup
library(here)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

source(here("R", "read_hh.R"))

my_sites <- c("DE-Lnf", "FI-Let", "US-Kon", "CN-Lch", "AU-Cpr")

snap_file <- list.files(here("data", "snapshots"), pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
snap <- read_csv(snap_file, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(site_id %in% my_sites)

# Einlesen der fünf Towers (mit Zwischenspeicher, damit das Rendern schneller ist)
cache <- here("data", "processed", "all_hh.rds")
if (file.exists(cache)) {
  all_hh <- readRDS(cache)
} else {
  zips <- list.files(here("data", "raw"), pattern = "\\.zip$", full.names = TRUE)
  all_hh <- bind_rows(lapply(zips, read_hh, exdir = here("data", "raw", "unzipped")))
  saveRDS(all_hh, cache)
}

# DE-Lnf has no _VUT_ NEE/GPP/RECO in its file: use the _CUT_REF variants instead
all_hh <- all_hh |>
  mutate(used_cut        = site == "DE-Lnf",
         NEE_VUT_REF     = if_else(used_cut, NEE_CUT_REF,     NEE_VUT_REF),
         NEE_VUT_REF_QC  = if_else(used_cut, NEE_CUT_REF_QC,  NEE_VUT_REF_QC),
         GPP_NT_VUT_REF  = if_else(used_cut, GPP_NT_CUT_REF,  GPP_NT_VUT_REF),
         RECO_NT_VUT_REF = if_else(used_cut, RECO_NT_CUT_REF, RECO_NT_VUT_REF))
```

# C1. Site overview

Data source: FLUXNET Shuttle snapshot `r basename(snap_file)`. File versions: `r paste(snap$fluxnet_product_name, collapse = "; ")`. Half-hourly time stamps are in local standard time (no daylight-saving shift).

```{r}
#| label: c1-table
overview <- snap |>
  transmute(Site = site_id, Name = site_name,
            Country = substr(site_id, 1, 2), IGBP = igbp,
            Lat = round(location_lat, 2), Lon = round(location_long, 2),
            `First year` = first_year, `Last year` = last_year,
            Hub = data_hub, Citation = product_citation)
kable(overview)
```

```{r}
#| label: c1-map
#| fig-cap: "Location of the five flux towers."
world <- map_data("world")
ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = world, aes(long, lat, group = group),
               fill = "grey90", colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data = snap, aes(location_long, location_lat), colour = "red", size = 3) +
  geom_text(data = snap, aes(location_long, location_lat, label = site_id),
            nudge_y = 6, size = 3.5) +
  coord_quickmap() +
  labs(x = "Longitude (°)", y = "Latitude (°)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# C2. Data coverage
```{r}
#| label: c2-coverage
#| fig-cap: "Share of half hours with measured NEE (NEE_VUT_REF_QC == 0) per site and year."
coverage <- all_hh |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(format(time, "%Y"))) |>
  group_by(site, year) |>
  summarise(share = mean(NEE_VUT_REF_QC == 0, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(coverage, aes(year, site, fill = share)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1), name = "Share measured") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2002, 2026, 2)) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Site") +
  theme_minimal()

best <- coverage |> arrange(desc(share)) |> slice(1)
```

Best coverage: site `r best$site` in `r best$year` (`r round(100 * best$share)` % of half hours measured).

For DE-Lnf, the delivered file contains no _VUT_ values for NEE, GPP and RECO. The _CUT_REF variants (constant USTAR threshold) were used instead (NEE_CUT_REF, GPP_NT_CUT_REF, RECO_NT_CUT_REF). DE-Lnf has no data in 2007–2009 and partial gaps in 2022–2023.


# C3. Summary statistics

Mean, minimum, maximum and share of missing half hours (`NA` after reading −9999) per site, computed from the half-hourly data. For precipitation (`P_F`), the mean is the **mean annual sum** over complete years; minimum and maximum are per half hour.

```{r}
#| label: c3-stats
#| results: asis
var_labels <- c(
  TA_F            = "Air temperature TA_F (°C)",
  SW_IN_F         = "Incoming shortwave SW_IN_F (W m⁻²)",
  VPD_F           = "Vapour pressure deficit VPD_F (hPa)",
  P_F             = "Precipitation P_F (mm yr⁻¹ mean; min/max in mm per 30 min)",
  NEE_VUT_REF     = "NEE_VUT_REF (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)",
  GPP_NT_VUT_REF  = "GPP_NT_VUT_REF (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)",
  RECO_NT_VUT_REF = "RECO_NT_VUT_REF (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)",
  H_F_MDS         = "Sensible heat H_F_MDS (W m⁻²)",
  LE_F_MDS        = "Latent heat LE_F_MDS (W m⁻²)"
)

long <- all_hh |>
  select(site, all_of(names(var_labels))) |>
  pivot_longer(-site, names_to = "var", values_to = "value")

stats <- long |>
  group_by(site, var) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            min  = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            max  = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            pct_missing = 100 * mean(is.na(value)),
            .groups = "drop")

# Mean annual precipitation sum (complete years only)
precip <- all_hh |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(format(time, "%Y"))) |>
  group_by(site, year) |>
  summarise(n = n(), annual = sum(P_F, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n >= 17520) |>
  group_by(site) |>
  summarise(p_annual = mean(annual), .groups = "drop")

stats <- stats |>
  left_join(precip, by = "site") |>
  mutate(mean = if_else(var == "P_F", p_annual, mean),
         Variable = factor(var_labels[var], levels = var_labels)) |>
  arrange(site, Variable)

for (s in my_sites) {
  cat("\n\n### ", s, "\n\n")
  tab <- stats |>
    filter(site == s) |>
    transmute(Variable, Mean = mean, Min = min, Max = max, `Missing (%)` = pct_missing)
  cat(kable(tab, digits = 2), sep = "\n")
}
```



# C4. Time series
Half-hourly data were aggregated to daily means (only days with all 48 half hours). Daily means in µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹ were multiplied by 1.0378 to get g C m⁻² d⁻¹ (× 86 400 s × 12.011 g mol⁻¹ × 10⁻⁶). Variables: `NEE_VUT_REF`, `GPP_NT_VUT_REF` (night-time partitioning) and `RECO_NT_VUT_REF`.

```{r}
#| label: c4-daily
conv <- 1.0378

daily <- all_hh |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(time)) |>
  group_by(site, date) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            NEE  = mean(NEE_VUT_REF, na.rm = TRUE) * conv,
            GPP  = mean(GPP_NT_VUT_REF, na.rm = TRUE) * conv,
            RECO = mean(RECO_NT_VUT_REF, na.rm = TRUE) * conv,
            .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n == 48) |>
  select(-n)

daily_long <- daily |>
  pivot_longer(c(NEE, GPP, RECO), names_to = "flux", values_to = "value")
```

```{r}
#| label: c4-plot
#| fig-cap: "Daily NEE, GPP and RECO (g C m⁻² d⁻¹) over the whole record, one panel per site."
#| fig-height: 10
ggplot(daily_long, aes(date, value, colour = flux)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~site, ncol = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Date (local standard time)",
       y = expression("Flux (g C " * m^-2 * " " * d^-1 * ")"),
       colour = "Flux") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Check of my aggregation against the daily `FLUXMET_DD` file of site US-Kon:

```{r}
#| label: c4-check
zip_kon <- list.files(here("data", "raw"), pattern = "US-Kon.*\\.zip$", full.names = TRUE)
dd_name <- grep("FLUXMET_DD", unzip(zip_kon, list = TRUE)$Name, value = TRUE)
unzip(zip_kon, files = dd_name, exdir = here("data", "raw", "unzipped"))

dd <- read_csv(file.path(here("data", "raw", "unzipped"), dd_name),
               na = "-9999", col_select = any_of(c("TIMESTAMP", "NEE_VUT_REF")),
               col_types = cols(TIMESTAMP = "c", .default = "d")) |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(TIMESTAMP, format = "%Y%m%d"))

cmp <- daily |>
  filter(site == "US-Kon") |>
  inner_join(dd, by = "date", suffix = c("_mine", "_dd"))

c(n_days = nrow(cmp),
  correlation = cor(cmp$NEE, cmp$NEE_VUT_REF, use = "complete.obs"),
  max_abs_diff = max(abs(cmp$NEE - cmp$NEE_VUT_REF), na.rm = TRUE))
```

data of C4 are coming from _CUT_

# C5. Diurnal cycles

Seasons are defined by meteorological months and **latitude**: for sites with latitude ≥ 0 (northern hemisphere) DJF = winter, MAM = spring, JJA = summer, SON = autumn. For AU-Cpr (latitude < 0, southern hemisphere) the seasons are shifted by six months (DJF = summer, JJA = winter, and so on). Hour of day is local standard time. Fluxes are half-hourly means over the whole record (NEE in µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹, LE in W m⁻²). For DE-Lnf, NEE is based on `NEE_CUT_REF`.

```{r}
#| label: c5-diurnal
#| fig-cap: "Mean diurnal cycle of NEE and LE per season, all five sites."
#| fig-height: 8
lat_tab <- snap |> select(site = site_id, lat = location_lat)

season_of <- function(month, lat) {
  s <- c("winter", "winter", "spring", "spring", "spring", "summer",
         "summer", "summer", "autumn", "autumn", "autumn", "winter")[month]
  south <- c(winter = "summer", spring = "autumn", summer = "winter", autumn = "spring")
  ifelse(lat < 0, south[s], s)
}

diurnal <- all_hh |>
  left_join(lat_tab, by = "site") |>
  mutate(month  = as.integer(format(time, "%m")),
         hour   = as.integer(format(time, "%H")) + as.integer(format(time, "%M")) / 60,
         season = factor(season_of(month, lat),
                         levels = c("winter", "spring", "summer", "autumn"))) |>
  group_by(site, season, hour) |>
  summarise(NEE = mean(NEE_VUT_REF, na.rm = TRUE),
            LE  = mean(LE_F_MDS, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_longer(c(NEE, LE), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(variable = recode(variable,
                           NEE = "NEE (µmol CO2 m-2 s-1)",
                           LE  = "LE (W m-2)"))

ggplot(diurnal, aes(hour, value, colour = site)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(variable ~ season, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Hour of day (local standard time)", y = "Mean flux", colour = "Site") +
  theme_minimal()
```

All sites show the expected diurnal pattern: NEE is positive at night (respiration) and turns negative during the day (net uptake), while LE follows the sun with a midday maximum. The amplitude is largest in summer, when US-Kon reaches the highest LE (about 300 W m⁻²) and DE-Lnf, CN-Lch and US-Kon reach midday NEE of about −17 to −19 µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹. FI-Let has a weaker summer uptake (about −11 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹), consistent with a boreal needleleaf forest. CN-Lch shows its strongest uptake and highest LE already in spring, which fits a cropland with a winter-wheat growing season. AU-Cpr has a much smaller cycle than the northern sites. Its strongest uptake and highest LE fall in its summer (DJF), which confirms that the southern-hemisphere season shift works.



# C6. Your reading

## Energy balance (US-Kon)

Only half hours with measured H and LE (`H_F_MDS_QC == 0`, `LE_F_MDS_QC == 0`) and available `NETRAD` and `G_F_MDS` are used.

```{r}
#| label: c6-energy
#| fig-cap: "US-Kon: H + LE against NETRAD − G (W m⁻²) for half hours with measured H and LE. Dashed line = 1:1, red line = linear fit."
eb <- all_hh |>
  filter(site == "US-Kon", H_F_MDS_QC == 0, LE_F_MDS_QC == 0) |>
  transmute(avail = NETRAD - G_F_MDS, turb = H_F_MDS + LE_F_MDS) |>
  filter(!is.na(avail), !is.na(turb))

fit <- lm(turb ~ avail, data = eb)
slope <- coef(fit)[["avail"]]

ggplot(eb, aes(avail, turb)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.05, size = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_abline(slope = slope, intercept = coef(fit)[["(Intercept)"]], colour = "red") +
  labs(title = "US-Kon",
       x = expression("NETRAD - G (W " * m^-2 * ")"),
       y = expression("H + LE (W " * m^-2 * ")")) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Number of half hours used: `r nrow(eb)`. Slope of the linear fit: `r round(slope, 2)` (R² = `r round(summary(fit)$r.squared, 2)`).

```{r}
#| label: c6-compare
conv <- 1.0378

annual <- all_hh |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(format(time, "%Y"))) |>
  group_by(site, year) |>
  filter(n() >= 17520, sum(!is.na(NEE_VUT_REF)) > 0.5 * n()) |>
  summarise(NEE_gC = mean(NEE_VUT_REF, na.rm = TRUE) * conv * 365, .groups = "drop")

comparison <- annual |>
  group_by(site) |>
  summarise(`Mean annual NEE (g C m-2 yr-1)` = mean(NEE_gC), n_years = n())

seasonal <- daily |>
  mutate(month = as.integer(format(date, "%m"))) |>
  group_by(site, month) |>
  summarise(GPP = mean(GPP, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(site) |>
  summarise(`GPP seasonal amplitude (g C m-2 d-1)` = max(GPP) - min(GPP))

gapfilled <- all_hh |>
  group_by(site) |>
  summarise(`Share not measured NEE (%)` = 100 * mean(NEE_VUT_REF_QC != 0, na.rm = TRUE))

kable(comparison |> left_join(seasonal, by = "site") |> left_join(gapfilled, by = "site"),
      digits = 1)
```

Among the five towers, the cropland CN-Lch takes up the most carbon, with a mean annual NEE of about −668 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹, followed by the broadleaf forest DE-Lnf (−608 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹, based on _CUT_ values). US-Kon (−116) and AU-Cpr (−195) are moderate sinks, and the needleleaf forest FI-Let is almost carbon neutral (−16 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹). The seasonal cycle, measured as the difference between the highest and lowest monthly mean GPP, is largest at CN-Lch (15.8 g C m⁻² d⁻¹), followed by US-Kon (13.4) and DE-Lnf (12.6), and by far the smallest at the savanna AU-Cpr (0.8). [Hier schreibst du selbst, was dich überrascht hat, z. B. dass FI-Let trotz Wald fast neutral ist oder dass AU-Cpr so wenig Jahresgang zeigt.] Between 50 % (AU-Cpr) and 72 % (FI-Let) of the half-hourly NEE values are not directly measured, meaning they are gap-filled or of lower quality (NEE_VUT_REF_QC != 0), so the annual sums depend strongly on the gap-filling. DE-Lnf has no _VUT_ values in its file, so _CUT_REF was used, and it has no data in 2007–2009 and partial gaps in 2022–2023. Annual sums include only years with more than half of the NEE values present, which is why DE-Lnf has 20 years instead of 23.

For DE-Lnf, the VUT (variable USTAR threshold) products are not available in the delivered file. The CUT (constant USTAR threshold) products were used instead. They differ only in how the turbulence threshold for night-time data is determined.

# Data and citation

**Snapshot and files:** `r basename(snap_file)`; `r paste(snap$fluxnet_product_name, collapse = "; ")`.

**Variables used:** `_VUT_REF` for NEE (`NEE_VUT_REF`), night-time partitioning for GPP and RECO (`GPP_NT_VUT_REF`, `RECO_NT_VUT_REF`), gap-filled meteorology (`_F`) and `H_F_MDS`, `LE_F_MDS`. Exception: for DE-Lnf the `_CUT_REF` variants were used because the `_VUT_` columns are empty. Time stamps are local standard time.

**Data citations:**

```{r}
#| results: asis
cat(paste0("- ", snap$site_id, ": ", snap$product_citation), sep = "\n")
```

**Method reference:** Pastorello, G. et al. (2020). The FLUXNET2015 dataset and the ONEFlux processing pipeline for eddy covariance data. *Scientific Data* 7, 225. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0534-3>

**Acknowledgement:** FLUXNET data products were produced and harmonized by eddy covariance regional networks and data
processing centers, including AmeriFlux, ChinaFlux, European Fluxes Database, ICOS, JapanFlux, KoFlux,
OzFlux, SAEON, and TERN. These products also include a modified version of ERA5 hourly data provided by
the Copernicus Climate Change Service.
